docs.label: The radio play (three speakers)
docs.text: And we're back. It's twelve forty on Night Radio, and line two has been blinking for ten minutes. Brom, are you there? [clears throat] I'm here. I'm here. Is this the radio? Am I on the radio? He's on the radio. You're on the radio, Brom. What's happening at the lighthouse tonight? Well, [sighs] the light went out. Not broken, mind you. It just stopped, like it wanted a nap. [laughs] A sleepy lighthouse. Pip, please. Brom, did you try turning it off and on again? Young man, I have kept that light for forty years. Of course I tried that. Ooh, ooh, I know. Play it a song. Lighthouses love songs. Do they? [laughs] Pip, cue the lullaby. Brom, hold the phone up to the lamp. It's, it's flickering. It's coming back. Would you look at that? [laughs] Yes. The power of radio. There you have it, night owls. Even lighthouses need a song sometimes. Good night, Brom. [laughs] Good night, you lot. Keep the music coming.

docs.label: The traffic report, in the noise
docs.text: Good evening. Here's the island traffic report. The night ferry is running ten minutes late because a seal is sleeping on the bow. The hill road is clear apart from one very slow tortoise near the bakery. And at the lighthouse, Graham reports one flickering lamp, now fixed with music. Drunk children again.

truth.scene:
Mo: [warmly] And we're back. It's twelve forty on Night Radio, and line two has been blinking for ten minutes. Bram, are you there?
Bram: [clears throat] I'm here, I'm here. Is this the radio? Am I on the radio?
Pip: [whispers] He's on the radio.
Mo: You're on the radio, Bram. What's happening at the lighthouse tonight?
Bram: Well. [sighs] The light went out. Not broken, mind you. It just... stopped. Like it wanted a nap.
Pip: [laughs] A sleepy lighthouse!
Mo: Pip, please. Bram, did you try turning it off and on again?
Bram: [offended] Young man, I have kept that light for forty years. Of course I tried that.
Pip: [excited] Ooh, ooh, I know! Play it a song! Lighthouses love songs.
Bram: [pause] ...Do they?
Mo: [laughs] Pip, cue the lullaby. Bram, hold the phone up to the lamp.
Bram: [far from the phone] It's... it's flickering. It's coming back! Would you look at that!
Pip: [cheering] Yes! The power of radio!
Mo: [softly] There you have it, night owls. Even lighthouses need a song sometimes. Goodnight, Bram.
Bram: [chuckles] Goodnight, you lot. Keep the music coming.
